goal: QuestInfiniteScan on-device layered radiance surface meshlets

A dedicated remote branch retains the exact hybrid code, old goal, and old DAG
The new implementation continues on a separate branch
evidence: Commit e9f37c1 preserves 304 files and the original 22-node hybrid/DiffSoup DAG
Remote branch origin/archive/hybrid-diffsoup-checkpoint-20260820 exists and tracks the immutable checkpoint

acceptance: Unity 6000.5.9f1 Android ARM64 Vulkan project builds
Meta XR permissions, tracking, passthrough bootstrap, and ADB deploy path remain available
Generated builds and caches stay outside the repository
evidence: Verification report /mnt/kingston-unity/Builds/Verification/20260820T132533Z/verification-report.json records successful Unity tests and Android/Vulkan build
The preserved fork deployed and scanned on the connected Quest 3/3S before the architecture pivot
Kingston-hosted Unity/build scripts remain under Tools/storage and Tools/unity

nodes.title: Retain versioned world, atomic store, pose graph, and transform foundations
acceptance: World/chunk manifests validate and round-trip rigid transforms
Atomic publication preserves the prior revision after interruption
Pose graph updates worldFromChunk without mutating local geometry
evidence: Runtime/World/WorldManifest*, WorldStore, PoseGraphModel, and PoseGraphOptimizer are present with deterministic EditMode coverage
The retained 93-test Unity checkpoint reports no failures, including manifest/store/pose tests
New meshlet page formats will version rather than reinterpret legacy TSDF payloads

nodes.title: Retain standards-compliant GLB/PBR writer foundations
acceptance: Chunk, sharded world, and bounded monolithic GLB paths exist
Pose-graph node transforms and honest metallic/roughness semantics are preserved
Official and independent validators are reproducible
evidence: Runtime/Export contains chunk/world GLB writers and atomic export controller
The retained verification report records zero Khronos errors/warnings and successful independent NodeIO validation

nodes.title: Freeze the on-device radiance-meshlet architecture and migration contracts
acceptance: Goal, DAG, decisions, state, resume tail, architecture spec, and AGENTS guardrails consistently name one production architecture
Reusable, replaceable, and removable code is mapped to concrete symbols
Buffer layouts, coordinate spaces, frame ownership, lifecycle states, quality gates, and migration order are explicit
Control-plane validation passes and the old DAG remains recoverable from the archive branch
evidence: AGENTS.md and .codex/GOAL.md freeze the pure Quest GPU/indirect mapper, monotonic quality contract, quantitative acceptance gates, and post-compaction guardrails

docs/architecture/RADIANCE_MESHLET_ARCHITECTURE.md defines coordinate/time ownership, GPU pass graph, draft aligned buffer capacities, dynamic geometry/appearance LOD, two-arena page lifecycle, UI boundary, and migration sequence
.codex/DECISIONS.md records the active ADR set and points superseded hybrid/DTSDF decisions to archive commit e9f37c1
The unintegrated DTSDF scaffold and obsolete directional decision were removed only from the new branch; the remote archive retains them
python3 Tools/validate_goal_state.py passes: 28 nodes, one active node, four reusable foundations done before this status transition

nodes.title: Implement immutable StereoRigFrame contracts and dual GPU camera capture
acceptance: One frame exposes RGB-L/R, depth-L/R, timestamps, intrinsics, extrinsics, poses, dimensions, and ownership without CPU color readback
Both passthrough camera streams are opened, permissioned, and disposed deterministically
Quest 3 and 3S capability differences are discovered at runtime rather than hard-coded
Unit tests cover contract validation, resource ownership, camera ordering, and unsupported capability failure

nodes.title: Implement frame synchronization, pose sampling, and capture diagnostics
acceptance: Configurable timestamp delta, pose age, tracking validity, and intrinsic-version gates fail closed
Depth and RGB timestamps are paired with the correct per-eye pose/extrinsics
Diagnostics report accepted/dropped frames, pair deltas, per-stream rates, latency, and failure reasons
Deterministic jitter/out-of-order/missing-eye tests prove no stale-frame fusion

nodes.title: Implement GPU depth consensus, normals, discontinuity mask, and confidence
acceptance: Left/right depth is reprojected with depth-dependent calibration and fused only when geometrically consistent
Confidence incorporates sensor validity, local noise, incidence, cross-eye agreement, temporal agreement, and tracking quality
Strong discontinuities suppress cross-edge fusion and rear-space carving
Captured fixtures and real-GPU parity tests cover planes, slants, silhouettes, poles, missing depth, and mixed pixels

nodes.title: Implement uncertain-tile scheduler and narrow stereo/temporal MVS
acceptance: Only uncertain/problem tiles enter refinement and work is bounded per frame
Native depth defines a narrow metric hypothesis interval with 8-16 candidates
Census/gradient cost uses the other eye and 2-4 pose-valid temporal observations
Left-right and temporal consistency reject ambiguous solutions rather than inventing geometry
Scheduling respects mapper GPU budget and thermal backpressure

nodes.title: Define packed surface, accumulator, meshlet, page, and memory contracts
acceptance: C# and HLSL layouts have explicit byte size/alignment and parity tests
Active records retain sufficient precision for point-to-plane solving; stable pages use chunk-local quantization with declared error bounds
Every buffer allocation is checked, no storage buffer exceeds 128 MiB, target active memory is <=1.2 GiB, and allocation fails closed before 2 GiB
Generation IDs and invalid sentinels prevent use-after-recycle
All live structures support GPU-only append/compact/scan plus indirect dispatch and draw arguments without CPU count readback

nodes.title: Implement bounded GPU layered-surface allocator and spatial index
acceptance: Chunk-local cells reference multiple surface layers without imposing voxel geometry resolution
Allocation, reuse, overflow, compaction, and generation validation are deterministic
Opposite normals and incompatible visibility can coexist in one spatial region
Stress tests hit capacity without memory corruption or unbounded growth

nodes.title: Implement hardware association raster for stable surface IDs
acceptance: Existing meshlets rasterize ID, predicted depth, normal, generation, and visibility into observation space
Association rejects depth, normal, generation, edge, and occlusion incompatibility
Unmatched valid observations are routed to new-layer candidates
Raster resources are double-buffered and never read while incomplete

nodes.title: Implement layered point-to-plane fusion and stable-surface protection
acceptance: Active surfaces update bounded information matrices/vectors with robust weights
Distance, incidence, confidence, visibility, dynamics, and residual history control fusion
A persistent information-quality envelope prevents lower-resolution, farther, blurrier, or more grazing observations from degrading stable geometry
Opposite-facing or occluded evidence never erases an existing layer
Near-then-far, far-then-near, grazing, thin-panel, pole, pipe, occlusion, dynamic-object, and noisy revisit tests pass
Stable close surfaces move <=2 mm under later lower-quality distant evidence

nodes.title: Implement local regularization, boundary ownership, and chunk-overlap blending
acceptance: Regularization improves compatible coplanar/curved support without crossing locked discontinuities or layers
Chunk overlap assigns deterministic surface ownership and avoids duplicate z-fighting
Boundary updates are local, budgeted, and revision-safe
Synthetic and captured seams remain continuous under pose-graph transform updates

nodes.title: Implement adaptive local meshlet topology with atomic publication
acceptance: Stable planar regions consolidate while curvature, silhouettes, thin features, and uncertain boundaries retain detail
Split/merge/stitch operations preserve layer identity, winding, manifold intent, and edge locks
Topology is built into an inactive generation and atomically swapped after validation
Fixed-capacity meshlets handle overflow without corrupting the published generation
No triangle bridges a strong depth discontinuity in accepted fixtures
GPU compaction and indirect arguments publish topology without CPU geometry traversal, count readback, or Unity Mesh rebuilding

nodes.title: Implement GPU-indirect world meshlet rendering and dynamic LOD
acceptance: Provisional and stable geometry use bounded ordinary Vulkan triangle rendering with depth testing and GPU-generated indirect draw lists
GPU frustum/occlusion culling and screen-space-error LOD select meshlet detail without CPU traversal
Geometry and appearance choose independent LOD so close inspection uses maximum captured detail while distant chunks remain cheap
Natural, Coverage, Geometry, Uncertainty, and Wireframe modes apply to active and persisted chunks
Published geometry remains spatially stable under head motion, chunk swaps, and pose-graph changes
Renderer never consumes retired or mutating generations and maintains 72 Hz target

nodes.title: Replace rollover with a nonblocking two-arena chunk lifecycle
acceptance: Current and next arenas overlap with Schmitt hysteresis in all axes including vertical travel
Source geometry remains published and visible while target mapping begins
Transition cannot outrun durable publication or strand multiple chunks in Finalizing
Dirty pages read back incrementally and no transition blocks the main thread >20 ms
Live mapping and rendering perform no synchronous readback; persistence uses only fenced asynchronous immutable page staging
Regression test reproduces and eliminates the archived four-rollover disappearance failure

nodes.title: Implement versioned meshlet-page persistence, streaming, reload, and revisit
acceptance: Surface, topology, appearance, observation, and quality pages publish atomically under a new schema
Last complete revision survives interruption, hash failure, cancellation, and app termination
Visible/near chunks dynamically rehydrate after eviction with bounded GPU/RAM residency
Revisit preserves stable layers and commits a monotonic revision
Legacy manifests remain read-only/migratable without reinterpreting TSDF bytes as new pages

nodes.title: Integrate pose graph, relocation, loop closure, and multi-floor worlds
acceptance: Tracking/overlap/loop constraints update only worldFromChunk
Active capture, association, renderer, export, and future observations use one coherent transform snapshot
Anchor relocation restores a world without flattening vertical topology
Long corridor loop and multi-floor fixtures converge without local-geometry mutation

nodes.title: Implement bounded observation reservoir and robust base-color fusion
acceptance: Chunk-local observations retain calibrated views by coverage, baseline, sharpness, exposure, and geometry support
Reservoir size is bounded and revisits replace weaker redundant evidence
Exposure-normalized color rejects occlusions, dynamics, blur, and grazing samples
Base color and confidence improve monotonically on accepted fixtures
A per-texel quality envelope preserves the sharpest valid close-range evidence and permits replacement only on measured information gain

nodes.title: Implement compact directional appearance and confidence-bearing PBR
acceptance: Incremental bounded least-squares state captures diffuse plus compact view-dependent residual
Geometric/detail normals carry confidence and do not hide unresolved geometry
Roughness is emitted only with adequate angular evidence; metallic stays zero when uncertain
Appearance update is time-sliced and does not require training, Python, CUDA, or network
Multiresolution GPU appearance pages support independently streamed texture LOD and retain maximum accepted texel detail

nodes.title: Adapt chunk and world GLB/PBR export to canonical meshlet pages
acceptance: Exporter consumes stable canonical meshlet generations rather than TSDF/refined/DiffSoup artifacts
Positions, normals, tangents, UV0, indices, base color, normal, and honest metallic-roughness semantics are correct
Selected chunk, sharded world, and bounded monolithic world preserve pose-graph transforms and revisions
Official validator and independent importer pass generated and physical fixtures

nodes.title: Replace debug-centric UI with the production scan workflow
acceptance: Primary navigation is Scan, Worlds, Quality, Export, and Settings; Diagnostics is an explicit developer view
Workflow state machine is Idle -> Permission/Warmup -> Scanning <-> Paused -> Finalizing -> Ready/Fault
Scan view exposes tracking, stereo sync/rates, mapping lag, stable geometry, unresolved edges, chunk, memory, and thermal health
Quality offers Fast/Balanced/Detail and honest geometry/appearance/material confidence
Legacy GS, server URL, DiffSoup, HQ-server refinement, freeze tint, and normal-operator clutter are absent

nodes.title: Remove legacy TSDF/DTSDF/Surface Nets/GS/DiffSoup/server production wiring
acceptance: Production scenes, assembly references, setup wizard, resources, shaders, UI, and package docs use only the new mapper
Unintegrated DTSDF scaffolding and scalar TSDF/Surface Nets mapping are removed from shipped code
Runtime.GSplat, HeavyCompute, DiffSoup renderer/client, and Python server are absent from the shipped package
Reusable representation-independent tests/tools remain, and archive branch provides full historical recovery
Clean Unity import and Android build prove no dangling serialization or shader references

nodes.title: Build the fixed captured/synthetic quality corpus and continuous verification gates
acceptance: Corpus covers planes, oblique walls, corners, 20/40 mm panels, round/square poles, pipes, rails, silhouettes, opposing faces, occlusion, exposure, dynamics, revisits, and vertical paths
Expected geometry, visibility, and confidence outcomes are versioned without committing private room imagery
CPU contract, GPU parity, failure injection, Unity, GLB, Android, and control-plane checks run from one verifier
Baseline comparison prevents regressions hidden by aggregate scores

nodes.title: Meet mapper performance, memory, thermal, and lifecycle gates
acceptance: Quest render stays 72 Hz and balanced mapping stays >=10 Hz
Mapper GPU p95 is <=4 ms amortized or an explicitly profiled quality fallback is selected
No buffer exceeds 128 MiB and active mapper memory stays <=1.2 GiB target / <2 GiB hard guard
Transitions show no >20 ms main-thread stall, synchronous/full-chunk readback, CPU mesh rebuild, premature resource retirement, or thermal runaway
GPU captures prove indirect culling/LOD/draw and no per-frame geometry readback in production
Profiles are retained outside git with machine-readable summaries in evidence

nodes.title: Pass physical Quest geometry, revisit, scale, offline, and export acceptance
acceptance: Accepted corpus measures median <=8 mm and p95 <=20 mm at 0.5-2.0 m with >=95% deliberate planar coverage
Thin structures, occlusion, discontinuities, near/far revisits, and material-confidence gates pass
At least 20 transitions plus return visits and a multi-floor route keep all chunks visible/reloadable with bounded residency
Scan/refine/restart/revisit/export work with networking disabled
Physical chunk/world GLBs validate and import with correct geometry, transforms, and PBR semantics

nodes.title: Finalize product docs, runbooks, clean verification, and publish the branch
acceptance: README, architecture, setup, operator, recovery, data-format, profiling, acceptance, and release docs describe the actual on-device product
Fresh clone/bootstrap/import/build/deploy/export runbook succeeds
Control validator, diff hygiene, secret scan, full verifier, and clean-tree checks pass
Implementation commits and final branch are pushed to origin without generated/private artifacts
